features.description: OpenCode is one open-source agent available as a terminal TUI, a desktop app, a web client, and a mobile app, all talking to a shared server.
Ships a provider and model catalog sourced from models.dev so most providers work after just connecting credentials.
Connect providers in the TUI or CLI via API key, OAuth, or command-based auth; each login becomes a saved, switchable account.
Add any OpenAI-compatible provider in opencode.json(c) with credential, runtime package, baseURL endpoint, headers, and merged request-body settings.
Use a ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription instead of an OpenAI API key; usage counts against the plan and shows no cost.
Connect GitHub Copilot through its device OAuth flow instead of an API key.

features.feature: Enterprise cloud providers (Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex)
features.description: First-class auth for Azure (Entra ID + deployment listings), Amazon Bedrock (AWS credential chain incl. SSO), and Google Vertex (Application Default Credentials).
Auto-discovers models from Ollama, LM Studio, and vLLM at their default local addresses; any OpenAI-compatible server can be configured manually.
Pick models per session via /models, per run via --model, or as a config default; variants like #high map to reasoning effort or token budgets.
OpenCode ships a set of free models usable without creating any account (hideable via OPENCODE_DISABLE_FREE_MODELS).
Cloud console with personal/team workspaces that centrally deliver models, policies, shared instructions and skills, members, SSO, SCIM, budgets, and billing to connected clients.
Flat subscription (Go/Go Plus/Go Teams) granting access to tested coding models with 5-hour/weekly/monthly usage limits, Extra Usage fallback, and an inference API endpoint.
Ordered wildcard rules per tool action and resource resolve to allow, deny, or ask; defaults block sensitive .env reads and let each agent layer narrower rules.
Ask-resolution dialogs offer 'Allow once' and 'Allow always', the latter saving the tool's proposed rule for future matching.
Permission checks for shell commands are decided by a built-in scanner that parses Bash, Zsh, POSIX sh, and PowerShell; unanalyzable commands fail closed.
Ordered policy statements can hard-deny providers, tools, MCP servers, skills, plugins, integrations, and web-search providers, with broader config overriding narrower.
Add stdio local servers and Streamable HTTP remote servers via `opencode mcp add` or mcp.servers config, with per-server timeouts and headers.
Remote servers sign in via OAuth with PKCE, discover the authorization server, refresh tokens, support pre-registered clients, and are managed with `opencode mcp auth`.
Pool one connection and tool list across projects with identical server settings; MCP resources are readable through built-in list/read tools under permission control.
Define agents in Markdown (frontmatter + body prompt) or JSONC with model, permissions, steps, hidden, and color; mode is primary, subagent, or all.
Ships a default Build primary agent, a read-mostly Plan primary, and General/Explore subagents; built-ins can be overridden or disabled by ID.
The built-in `plan` agent explores and plans without editing normal project files (writes only OpenCode plan files, shell still permission-gated).
A `subagent` tool starts child sessions with a configured subagent, its own model and permissions; subagent runs appear in the composer and are steerable.
Agent Skills (SKILL.md + bundled scripts/references) load from global, project, ~/.claude/skills compat, and HTTP catalog sources; model-triggered with permission rules.
Hierarchical AGENTS.md loading from workspace toward home plus a global file, with CLAUDE.md fallback in directories lacking AGENTS.md and live updates during a session.
The `instructions` config array adds extra files, glob patterns, or HTTP(S) URL guidance alongside discovered AGENTS.md files.
Slash commands from ~/.config/opencode/commands or .opencode/commands with $ARGUMENTS/$1..$n placeholders, !`shell` output blocks, and agent/model frontmatter.
A command with `subagent: true` runs in a background child session instead of the current conversation.
Load npm, Git, or local plugins that add tools, hooks, integrations, commands, and agents; managed via `opencode plugin add/list/check/update/remove`.
Plugins exporting ./gui-experimental add panels, commands, or settings to OpenCode Desktop; desktop plugins can be created, installed, and shared.
Terminal plugins are configured separately in cli.json and keep working when the CLI connects to a remote server.
Per-step filesystem snapshots stored in an internal Git database power /undo (revert conversation + file changes, prompt returns to composer) and /redo.
Continue the last session with -c/--continue (TUI, mini, or run) or pick any session via /sessions, Ctrl+O, or `opencode session list`.
Sessions can be forked from a message (session.fork keybind) and via session/fork over ACP, with a fork-notice plugin on new forks.
`opencode session export` (optionally --sanitize) and `opencode session import` move session data as JSON between machines.
Ctrl+P opens a command palette exposing every action; slash commands (/new, /sessions, /models, /agents, /undo, /redo, /edit) are typed with / filtering.
@-search attaches files with line ranges, ! enters shell mode, /btw asks side questions that don't enter the conversation, and prompts can queue while the agent works.
30+ built-in themes (opencode, catppuccin, tokyonight, dracula, ...), a system theme derived from the terminal palette, light/dark/system modes, and custom JSON themes.
Every keybind is configurable in cli.json with a leader key (default Ctrl+X), a diff viewer (d switches source), stash, tabs, and a which-key hint panel.
Persistent tab strip (Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+T) with per-cwd or global scope, shared across clients connected to the same server.
`opencode mini` is a minimal inline interface that prints replies into normal scrollback with its own config group.
`opencode run` submits a prompt non-interactively with --model, --continue, --format json (newline-delimited) and --file attachments; documented pattern for CI with API-key secrets.
Run the CLI with --auto to allow every action you haven't explicitly denied.
A shared per-user background server owns sessions, config, integrations, permissions, and tool execution; every local client connects to it and it's managed via `opencode service`.
Runs the API and web server in the foreground with --hostname/--port/CORS control, OPENCODE_PASSWORD basic-auth, and Docker/systemd-friendly standalone deployment.
`opencode api` calls server endpoints or operation IDs (e.g. GET /api/session) against the running server for scripting and integrations.
One-time pairing links plus a QR code sign a browser or app into the server within 5 minutes; over SSH use port forwarding, or `opencode pair --remote` via OpenTunnel from any network.
OpenCode Mobile (iOS TestFlight beta, Google Play) pairs via `opencode pair --remote` QR, lists and steers the computer's live sessions, and supports voice calls where the agent answers out loud.
Native desktop app for macOS/Windows/Linux with parallel agents in tabs, live app preview in a browser pane, diff viewers, and multi-device session pickup.

OpenCode Browse is a Chrome extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, and more) that lets the agent use your real browser with your logins and tabs, incl. handoffs and tab lending; works with OpenCode and other MCP clients.
`opencode acp` speaks the Agent Client Protocol over stdin/stdout for editor integrations (e.g. Zed), supporting session load/resume/fork, permission prompts, and per-session MCP servers.
Marketplace extension for VS Code and forks (Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium): Cmd+Esc split-terminal launch, selection/tab context sharing, and file-reference shortcuts.

features.feature: VS Code extension for v2 (OpenCode Beta)
features.description: 'OpenCode Beta' (sst-dev.opencode-v2) is the VS Code Marketplace extension for OpenCode 2, published by SST.
Automatic summary compaction near the context limit keeps ~15k recent tokens, writes summaries in the background, supports a separate summary model, and enables provider-native compaction.
Optional warming sends background keep-alive requests just before each model's prompt cache expires to keep caching effective.
Built-in web search through Exa, Firecrawl, Parallel, or Tavily keys, or 'random' failover on HTTP 429, with per-query permission rules.
Attach local files, directories, or images (auto-resized, up to 20 MiB) via @ references or client pickers; webfetch retrieves URLs as markdown/text/html.
Files are formatted after write/edit/patch using built-in gofmt/prettier/biome/etc. or custom commands matched by extension.
Named context sources from local directories or remote Git repositories are auto-cloned and attachable by alias, with descriptions in agent instructions.
Default tool-calling style: the model runs JavaScript via the `execute` tool to call and combine catalog tools (incl. MCP tools) for parallel, cheap orchestration.
Core tools: read, glob, grep, edit, write, patch, shell, webfetch, websearch, question, skill, subagent, execute, plus session rename/move and Git worktree management.
Experimental image generate/edit tool appears when a connected provider has an image model, saving results into the project.
A browser Code Mode namespace controls the browser attached by the desktop app (open tabs, navigate, capture) for agent-driven browser work.
Sessions can create, list, and remove Git worktrees for the project, or move into one, isolating parallel agent work.
Layered system/global/project JSON(C) config with a published JSON schema for editor validation and autocomplete, covering model, agent, permissions, policies, and more.
One global terminal-client settings file controls theme, animations, tabs, diffs, alerts/notifications, sounds, mouse, keybinds, mini, and TUI plugins.
Proxy/auth env vars for the service, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for private CAs, and per-provider mutual-TLS client certificates.
Official versioned Docker images (ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:2.0.0) for running OpenCode as a server in containers.

`opencode stats` (shareable usage statistics), `opencode upgrade` self-updates, `opencode debug` paths/config tooling, `opencode reload` live config reload, and `opencode auth export/import` moves credentials between machines.
